summary: BBN's host status report for December 20 to 30, 1971, noting that the Lincoln Labs TX2 became a server. It was updated by RFC 293.

plainLanguage.summary: This report records which ARPANET computers answered tests during a two-week period. It also lists which computers offered services and which were intended only to use services.

subtitle: A BBN snapshot of ARPANET host availability from December 20 to 30, 1971.

tldr.problem: People using the early network needed to know which hosts were available to provide services.
tldr.mechanism: BBN attempted connections from a Terminal IMP and recorded the results alongside each host's reported status or prediction.
tldr.outcome: The Lincoln Labs TX2 became a server during this reporting period. RFC 288 obsoletes RFC 287 and was updated by RFC 293.

today: RFC 288 is listed as Unknown. It obsoletes RFC 287 and was updated by RFC 293.

sections.title: The Reporting Period
sections.content:
This report covers the status of most Network Hosts from December 20 to December 30. BBN did not test on December 24 or December 31 because of its Christmas and New Year's observances. The report notes that the Lincoln Labs TX2, Network Address 112, became a server during this period.

The report is a dated operational snapshot. It includes both test results and status predictions supplied by people at the listed sites.
sections.plainLanguage: The report shows which hosts responded during the listed test period. It also notes that the Lincoln Labs TX2 began acting as a server.

sections.title: Hosts Excluded from Daily Tests
sections.content:
The report excludes hosts not expected to function regularly as servers for at least two weeks. It also excludes hosts intended to be users only. These include Terminal IMPs, the Network Control Center computer used to gather network statistics, and several site computers listed in the RFC.

The BBN Terminal IMP at Network Address 158 is a prototype. It is often disconnected because its programs are being refined and debugged. A star in the tables marks hosts not included in daily testing.
sections.plainLanguage: Some hosts were left out because they were not expected to provide regular service or were intended only to use other hosts. The report marks these exclusions in its tables.

sections.title: Test Results and Their Meaning
sections.content:
One table lists each host's network address, site, computer, reported status or prediction, and the person who supplied it. Other tables record tests by date and time. A hash mark means the site had warned that its system might not be available at that time.

The result codes distinguish an open and accessible host, a dead or inaccessible host, a connection that opened only briefly, a refusal, and a timeout. A timeout means the host did not complete the Initial Connection Protocol (ICP) and open a connection within 60 seconds. The BBN Terminal IMP could not test the UCLA IBM-360/91's NETRJS service, so the report treated a connection to its logger as evidence that the service worked.
sections.plainLanguage: The tables use short codes to show what happened during each test. A timeout means the host did not finish the connection process within 60 seconds.

items.label: Dead
items.desc: Host was dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP.

items.label: Half open
items.desc: Host opened a connection, then closed it or stopped responding.

items.label: Open
items.desc: Host opened a connection and was accessible to users.

items.label: Refused
items.desc: Host returned a CLS to the initial RFC.

items.label: Timed out
items.desc: Host did not complete the ICP and open a connection within 60 seconds.

references.text: RFC 287, the earlier host status report obsoleted by this RFC.
